item.title: Italy stun France 3-1 to hand Zidane first defeat as Les Bleus coach
item.description: Italy came from behind to beat France 3-1 in Milan and hand Zidane his first defeat since taking charge of Les Bleus. France were without Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele due to injury but Michael Olise pounced on a loose pass from Gianluigi Donnarumma to fire them ahead on 10 minutes. Francesco Pio Esposito steered in Nicolo Cambiaghi’s pass to bring Italy level before France twice hit the post through Bradley Barcola and Rayan Cherki. Sebastiano Esposito blazed a second-half penalty wide for Italy, but Roberto Mancini’s side did not rue that miss as Davide Frattesi powered home Federico Dimarco’s cut-back. Francesco Pio Esposito then doubled his tally for the night, succeeding where his older brother had failed by converting a penalty after Dayot Upamecano fouled substitute Antonio Vergara. Italy climbed above France at the top of Group A1 on head-to-head record. Both teams have 10 points going into the final round of games, with Belgium just one point adrift. Belgium host Italy on Sunday and France are at home to Turkey. Turkey slid to a fifth straight loss as they went down 2-1 to Belgium in Izmir. Arda Guler’s magnificent free-kick put Turkey ahead under new coach and former midfielder Sergen Yalcin, but Belgium struck twice in quick succession with goals from Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere to come away with victory. item.title: Spain beat Czech Republic to retain perfect Nations League record
item.description: Alex Baena scored from the spot and Marc Pubill added another seconds from time as Spain beat ten-men Czech Republic 2-0 in the Nations League in Prague on Thursday. The win leaves Spain unbeaten in 44 competitive games in a row, including five wins in as many Nations League games this season. Spain, who already secured a quarter-final berth before travelling to Prague, will face England in Madrid on Sunday in their final Group A3 game. Baena scored on 39 minutes after a VAR check revealed Czech midfielder Lukas Ambros had handled the ball inside the box. The Atletico Madrid winger blasted his spot kick past Matej Kovar who touched the ball but failed to clear it. Czech captain Ladislav Krejci was sent off in the 69th minute after bringing down second-half substitute Roberto Fernandez on a counter-attack. It was a deja-vu for the Wolverhampton defender who also got a red card at the end of Spain’s 3-1 home win over the Czechs last month. Pubill, another substitute, beat Kovar with a low shot deep into stoppage time after the Czech back four left him alone facing the Eindhoven goalkeeper. Luis de la Fuentes missed Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Rodri and Eric Garcia over injuries while Mikel Oyarzabal was sidelined with flu for the Prague game. Spain got off to a slow start on the chilly evening but never really let the hosts get close throughout the first half. They gradually stepped up their pressure, often confining the Czechs to their box and looking for chances. Fabian Ruiz hit the post with a curling right-footer three minutes from halftime, while Dean Huijsen’s header found Kovar’s arms. Yeremy Pino, replacing Yamal on the right flank, saw his goal overturned by VAR for offside just two minutes into the second half. The Czechs showed higher spirits after the break, but David Zima tipped the ball over the bar from close range on 50 minutes and Adam Hlozek’s glancing header landed on the top of the crossbar. The Czechs lost momentum after the red card, but Baena had two efforts cleared by Kovar who also denied Fernandez from close range. The hosts, led by de la Fuente’s long-time collaborator Santi Denia, have lost all their Nations League games this season. They are next travelling to Croatia for a game they need to win to stay in the top tier of the competititon for the next edition. item.title: Record-breaking Kane fires England into Nations League knockouts
item.description: Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking 126th England appearance with a goal from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 on Thursday to book a place in the Nations League quarter-finals. Slaven Bilic’s team were determined to avoid the embarrassment of their 7-0 mauling by England in Rijeka last month and looked much more solid from the kick-off. But goals from Morgan Rogers and captain Kane kept England second in their group, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March. Neither side got out of second gear in the opening stages of the match at Wembley. Elliot Anderson fired over in the 16th minute and Croatia’s Josip Misic flashed a shot wide midway through the first half. Chelsea forward Rogers broke the deadlock in the 24th minute in slightly fortuitous fashion following a neat move by the home side. Kane floated a ball to Jude Bellingham on the right of the penalty area and the Real Madrid man cushioned the ball first time across the area towards Rogers. Manchester City’s Josko Gvardiol had a chance to clear but got in a tangle and Chelsea’s Rogers poked the ball past goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic. England started to find some rhythm as they went in search of a second goal but failed to add to their tally before half-time. Thomas Tuchel’s men were again the more potent team at the beginning of the second period. But the visitors levelled against the run of play just before the hour mark after a glaring error by England defender Jarell Quansah, who misdirected a header from close range towards Jordan Pickford following a Croatia corner. The ball fell to Petar Sucic, who stabbed home. Minutes later England were back in front, with Bayer Leverkusen defender Quansah again at the heart of the action after his shirt was tugged in the penalty area. Referee Morten Krogh initially did not award a penalty but he was sent to the monitor by the VAR and pointed to the spot. Kane made no mistake, drilling home for record-extending 92nd England goal. Nikola Vlasic gave England a scare, firing just wide of Jordan Pickford’s goal as Croatia showed they were still alive. James Garner thought he had scored a third for England after a Bellingham cut-back but Bellingham was in an off-side position when he received the ball. Ballon d’Or winner Kane won his 126th cap when the game kicked off — taking him clear of his tie with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton. A giant banner was raised before kick-off with a picture of the 33-year-old and the words “England’s Finest”. Shilton was part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions skipper, along with Football Association patron Prince William. England remain second in Nations League Group A3, after leaders Spain beat the Czech Republic 2-0 but are now assured of a place in the quarter-finals. Spain and England face each other in Madrid on Sunday. The post Record-breaking Kane fires England into Nations League knockouts appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Online safety concerns are reshaping how people meet strangers
item.description: It’s hard to ignore how meeting new people online has changed in the past decade. With so many platforms connecting millions, the possibilities feel endless, but the risks have become more visible too. Stories about scams, harassment, and data breaches are everywhere, and they’ve made people think twice before reaching out to someone they don’t know. Safety concerns aren’t just in the background anymore—they’re shaping the way we start conversations, choose platforms, and decide how much to share. As awareness grows, so do new habits and expectations for digital introductions. This shift doesn’t just affect individuals; it’s influencing whole communities as we all adapt to a more cautious, connected world. Changing first steps: why some users now engage with strangers differently online That growing caution is easy to spot in the way people now approach first interactions with strangers online. Instead of jumping right into open conversations, many start by looking for platforms that let them control who they talk to, or give them the option to remain anonymous until they feel comfortable. Features like one-click exit buttons, video previews, or private chat rooms have become popular for exactly this reason. Women, in particular, are leading this change. They’re more likely to say safety is a top concern, which shows up in everything from avoiding certain apps to using aliases or insisting on in-app messaging only. The choice of platform matters too. Video chat sites, for example, offer a sense of control because users can see and hear who they’re talking to—and can leave the conversation instantly if something doesn’t feel right. It highlights how both optimism and skepticism shape the way people meet and interact online now. Safety in practice: behaviors and community responses on Nigerian social platforms That skepticism and caution show up in everyday choices for users in Nigeria too. People still want to meet, form friendships, and build relationships across digital spaces, even as they weigh the risks involved. High-profile actions like WhatsApp bans scam accounts show that companies are working to remove bad actors and create safer environments. These crackdowns send a message that security isn’t optional, but a shared responsibility between users and service providers. Even with new tools and policies, the tension between wanting to connect and needing to protect yourself is likely to stay. Ongoing education, clear safety features, and active moderation will remain important as the way we meet strangers online continues to evolve. item.title: UNN Deaths: Gov Mbah mourns, orders investigation
item.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr Peter Mbah, has expressed deep grief over the deaths of four students of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, UNN, who reportedly died during an off-campus sign-out party organised for one of their friends, describing the incident as a heartbreaking loss. Mbah described the deaths as a grievous loss, not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to Enugu State as a whole. He called for a ban on sign-out parties among undergraduates, noting that the practice had brought too much sorrow to families and tertiary institutions across the country. This was contained in a press statement issued by the governor’s media aide, Mazi Uche Anichukwu, on Thursday. “I received with rude shock and deep sense of loss the news of the off-campus sign-out party leading to the death of four students of the University of Nigeria Nsukka, and hospitalisation of six others. “This is a grievous loss not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to us as a state. Losing them in their prime and along with their promising future cuts as deeply as a sharp knife. We, therefore share in this grief and pray God to grant their families, friends, and the UNN community the equanimity to bear the heartbreaking loss. “Our hearts go out to their parents in particular, who sacrificed personal comforts to sponsor their children through the university, but only to face this sad turn of events. “As a government, we have ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding their deaths and will work closely with the university authorities and security agencies to get to the roots of the sad development and forestall a recurrence. “In the meantime, I have suspended my scheduled town hall meeting with the UNN community on Friday, November 13, 2026, as we join the university in mourning the dead. “Going forward, we will work with the authorities of tertiary institutions to enforce a full ban on sign-out parties and other excessive celebrations, a trend that has cost more lives and brought more sorrows than joy to families and higher institutions of learning,” the governor stated. Mbah also called for increased public enlightenment campaigns by relevant agencies and institutions on the consequences of drug use and abuse. He prayed for the peaceful repose of the souls of the deceased. The post UNN Deaths: Gov Mbah mourns, orders investigation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: By Henry Umoru AHEAD of 2027 Presidential and general elections, the Senate has condemned in very strong terms, cases of political violence, attacks and disruption of political activities across the country. item.title: AFCONQ: Why I didn’t invite Maduka Okoye – Chelle
item.description: Super Eagles head coach Eric Chelle has explained his decision to leave goalkeeper Maduka Okoye out of Nigeria’s squad for their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches. Chelle, who is preparing the Super Eagles for their double-header against Tanzania, said his selection decisions were based on considerations both on and off the pitch. The Franco-Malian tactician insisted that the national team was not obligated to any particular player, stressing that his choices were guided by his assessment of what was best for the squad. “The national team is not close to him or anyone. I made my choice and when I made my choice I made it around the pitch and outside it,” Chelle said. Okoye, who plays for Italian club Udinese, has been absent from recent Super Eagles selections, with Stanley Nwabali, Francis Uzoho and Arthur Okonkwo among the goalkeepers considered by the coach. Chelle’s latest comments underline his position that selection for the national team is based on his technical and other considerations rather than a player’s reputation or status. The Super Eagles are seeking to strengthen their position in the AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign as they prepare to face Tanzania in two crucial Group L encounters. item.title: AFCON 2027Q: Guinea-Bissau drop points, hand Super Eagles chance to close gap
item.description: Nigeria’s Super Eagles have received a boost in their quest to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations after Guinea-Bissau were held to a 1-1 draw by Madagascar in their Group L encounter on Thursday. The result offers Nigeria an opportunity to reduce the gap at the top of the group following Guinea-Bissau’s impressive start to the qualifying campaign. The Djurtus had taken control of Group L after recording a 3-0 victory over the Super Eagles in their Matchday Two encounter last month. However, they were unable to maintain their winning run against Madagascar, needing a late goal to salvage a point. Warren Caddy gave Madagascar the lead a minute before the hour mark, putting Guinea-Bissau under pressure. But Galatasaray forward Renato Nhaga came to the visitors’ rescue, scoring six minutes from time to secure a 1-1 draw. The result leaves Guinea-Bissau top of Group L with seven points from three matches, while Madagascar sit third with two points. Nigeria can take advantage of the dropped points when they host Tanzania’s Taifa Stars in Uyo on Friday. A victory would strengthen the Super Eagles’ position in the group and provide a much-needed boost to their qualification hopes after their heavy defeat to Guinea-Bissau. The encounter is therefore crucial for Nigeria as they seek to get their AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign back on track. Amupitan spoke on Thursday at Chatham House, London, at a dialogue held with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI) on the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” His Chief Press Secretary, Adedayo Oketola, said the INEC chairman noted that the controversies over the 2023 presidential election badly dented public confidence in the commission. “First, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC—damage so large that the Commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said. He said the commission’s audit after 2023 traced the worst result management failures to collation centres, not polling units. “In 2023, there were instances of inaccurate results or results with over-voting being uploaded onto IReV. We have now devised a technical safeguard: if a result is not accurate at the polling unit, it will not go to IReV at all. The moment a result appears on IReV, citizens can trust what they see. By eliminating inconsistencies at the source, collation will become a transparent formality”, he stated. The INEC chairman announced that the commission would hold a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28, 2026. “On the 28th of this month, we will conduct a mock accreditation and voting exercise across all states of the federation to simulate the presidential election and verify that we have gotten both accreditation and electronic result transmission right,” he said. Asked why Nigerians should trust his leadership, Amupitan who assumed office in October 2025, pointed to the off-cycle elections he had conducted. “Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said. He listed the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, the Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections. Amupitan recalled that the 2021 Anambra governorship poll took roughly five days to conclude, whereas results in Anambra and Osun were declared the day after voting under his watch. “Every election is a lesson. The 2023 general election was a major lesson for Nigeria, and the Anambra election was another,” he said. He said INEC considered introducing a new electoral technology for 2027 but chose to upgrade its existing infrastructure because of the tight timeline before the polls. To address the malfunctions of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) linked to heat and storage conditions in 2023, he said INEC was building climate-controlled storage facilities in all states. The commission has also bought extra devices and cut the maximum number of voters assigned per BVAS from 1,250 to 850, so that polling units with more than 850 registered voters will get multiple devices. On funding, Amupitan said INEC had received a substantial part of its 2027 election budget and had been assured that the outstanding balance, part of which is meant for the recruitment and welfare of ad hoc staff, would be released before the end of November. Responding to allegations on social media that linked his phone number to a controversial X account, he denied ever operating one. He said an independent forensic review had been obtained and the matter referred to the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Inspector-General of Police for investigation. He dismissed suggestions that his past legal representation in political disputes would affect his impartiality. “My loyalty is solely to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the Electoral Act,” he said. On claims of an 85 per cent surge in registrants in a ward in Ebonyi State, he said the commission had investigated and resolved the complaint in line with statutory procedures. The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on January 16, 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections follow on February 6, 2027. Amupitan urged young Nigerians to stay involved in the democratic process. “Misinformation remains one of the greatest threats to our democracy. Citizens must verify information before acting or sharing, and give our democracy the chance to succeed,” he said. item.title: Scaloni to stay on as Argentina coach until 2030 World Cup
item.description: Lionel Scaloni on Thursday agreed to stay on as coach of Argentina’s national football team until after the 2030 World Cup, ending the doubts that had been swirling since this year’s World Cup final defeat. Scaloni’s decision to renew his contract was announced by Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia at a press conference with the 48-year-old manager. Scaloni, who took the Albiceleste to victory at the 2022 tournament in Qatar, told reporters he was as enthusiastic as “on day one”. “A new project begins now,” he said a month after Lionel Messi, the team’s leading light for 20 years, bowed out of international football. Tapia said that Scaloni would be the Argentina manager with the most World Cups under his belt by the time his contract ended. Scaloni had cast doubt on his future with the team after Argentina’s 1-0 defeat by Spain in a bad-tempered July 19 World Cup final in New Jersey. He has been coach for eight years, taking over in September 2018, after a traumatic World Cup in Russia, where Argentina were eliminated in the round of 16. Scaloni took over one of the most prestigious jobs in football without any prior experience and built the team into one widely considered the best in Argentine history. Besides the 2022 World Cup he coached Argentina to two Copa America titles, in 2021 and 2024. He now faces the task of taking the team forward without his 39-year-old talisman Messi. “What must remain is this team spirit, this feeling of unity among the players and the people,” he said after losing the final to Spain. item.title: 2027: Tinubu will lose if he contests against anybody picked on street — Dalung
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Solomon Dalung has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would lose the 2027 election even if his opponent were “anybody picked on the street,” arguing that the President was afraid of facing voters. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Dalung made the prediction while responding to a question about how the opposition could overcome the APC’s resources amid the current internal leadership and legal crisis in the ADC. He nevertheless insisted the party was ready to challenge Tinubu at the ballot. “Since my experience in politics, like I always say, Nigerians, I was brought into politics at a much tender age. I have never seen a weak president in an election like Bola Ahmed Tinubu. If you drag anybody on the street and put him on a ballot at a contest with Tinubu, he will defeat him,” Dalung said. He claimed Tinubu was apprehensive about the election despite having been in office for four years, and challenged the President and APC to let the contest be decided by voters. “Bola Tinubu is so scared, having been in office for four years, he is so scared of election. And all we are seeing in ADC, let’s meet at the ballot. You claim it was the ballot that brought you to power, let’s meet at the ballot,” he said. Dalung also accused the APC of obstructing opposition parties’ campaign activities, alleging that venues had been closed, hotels taken over and party offices sealed. He compared the situation with the 2014 election period, saying the APC would have been left with few places to campaign if it had faced similar restrictions then. “Nobody will be blamed except Tinubu. Why? Because I mean, in the history of Nigeria, we have seen opposition parties contest election, but we have never seen this type of situation. If the PDP in 2014 were closing venues for rallies and taking over hotels, sealing party offices, the APC would have no place to campaign except the streets,” he said. He argued that moving the opposition onto the streets would not weaken its campaign, claiming those attending its gatherings were genuine supporters rather than people hired to fill rallies. “Now, for Tinubu and his APC to move the opposition on pit, they have lost the election. This is because the people we are having on the street are organic followers. Those are the Nigerians that will vote. They are not rented crowds from all over the federation,” Dalung said. item.description: By By Henry Umoru, and Gift ChapiOdekina The House of Representatives, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) have condemned reported cases of political violence across the country following an attack on NDC supporters during a town hall meeting in Lagos. While the NDC demanded an immediate investigation, arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the attack in Lagos, the APC-PCC also condemned the incident and called on security agencies to apprehend the perpetrators. item.title: De Miguel death made me thank God over Zidane headbutt — Materazzi
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Italy defender Marco Materazzi says the death of Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel after an on-field collision made him reflect on the headbutt he suffered from Zinedine Zidane in the 2006 World Cup final. Materazzi said the incident, one of football’s most infamous World Cup moments, still troubled him 20 years later. He told Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport that De Miguel’s death made him grateful he had escaped serious injury. “The death of Jesus de Miguel made me thank God that nothing had happened to me,” Materazzi said in an interview published on Thursday. De Miguel, a Tenerife striker, died after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Segunda Division match earlier this month. Zidane, then captain of France, was sent off for headbutting Materazzi in the chest during the 2006 final, which Italy won on penalties. Zidane, now France coach, said last month he was not proud of the headbutt but did not regret it. Materazzi said he and Zidane appeared to put the episode behind them when they met before a match in 2010, although Zidane later disputed Materazzi’s account of the encounter. “When he saw me, he hesitated a little, he even turned to walk back,” Materazzi said. “But I approached him and shook his hand: ‘I’m glad we’re meeting here, where nobody can see us.’ “He replied: ‘Don’t worry, these things happen, it’s all in the past.’ It’s a shame he later denied everything, saying he thought I was a fan.” France are scheduled to play Italy in the Nations League later on Thursday. item.title: 2027: Opposition parties lack experience to govern Nigeria, says Ambode
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State Governor, Akinwunmi Ambode, has criticised opposition parties seeking to unseat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections, saying they lack the political experience and leadership depth required to govern Nigeria. Ambode specifically mentioned the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and other opposition platforms, arguing that the APC had greater political experience and ideological consistency. He spoke at the APC East Senatorial District rally held at Epe Recreational Ground, Epe, Lagos State, where he canvassed support for President Bola Tinubu, the party’s Lagos governorship candidate, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, and other APC candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Ambode said the APC had remained consistent in its political identity, unlike some politicians who, according to him, frequently moved from one political party to another. “APC is our party. We are a collective of the progressives. We have been consistent and delivering for the party. Over the years, we have remained with the progressives and we do not move from one party to another like other people,” he said. Describing the APC as a party connecting the country’s past, present and future, the former governor argued that its political experience placed it in a different position from opposition parties seeking to take over the reins of government. He also credited Tinubu’s political vision and record as Lagos governor with contributing to the state’s economic and infrastructural development, particularly its emergence as a major investment destination. Ambode said the foundations laid during Tinubu’s tenure as governor helped create an environment for financial institutions and corporate organisations to establish and expand their operations in Lagos. “Whether you like him or not, he is a visionary leader. If not for Tinubu, who laid the foundation for the Lagos of today, all the financial firms that have their headquarters in Lagos would have been struggling to survive. But today, his vision has assisted the country to remain an investor destination,” he said. He urged Lagos residents and Nigerians across different social and economic backgrounds to support the APC in the forthcoming elections. Ambode also appealed to members of the Igbo community living in Lagos and other parts of the country to consider national unity and their economic interests when making political choices. “To my Igbo brothers, wherever you live and get your prosperity, that is where you should call home. The former top civil servant also promised to create 200,000 youth employment opportunities and 5,000 enterprise opportunities annually, alongside a ₦19.2bn agricultural production fund to provide affordable financing and inputs to farmers and cooperatives. He said the proposed ₦100bn security trust fund would finance intelligence-led operations, strengthen community partnerships, equip security agencies and improve coordination among security formations to address insecurity across the state. Kawu said his decision to prioritise security was informed by his visit to Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area, where he witnessed the aftermath of attacks and the suffering of residents. Sulaiman Bolakale Kawu “One of the most painful experiences in my entire life was my visit to Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area of our state. I stood before the destruction. I saw blood on the ground. I witnessed firsthand the pain and fear of a traumatised community,” he said. He added that the experience reinforced his determination to ensure that residents could live and conduct their businesses without fear of attacks, kidnapping and other criminal activities. “As Governor, I will not rest or sleep when the life of any Kwaran is under threat,” the PDP candidate said. On workers’ welfare, Kawu promised to introduce a 13th-month salary for all civil servants in the state, assuring that salaries and other entitlements would be paid promptly. “As a retired public servant myself, I understand the sacrifices, expectations and challenges of workers. I will ensure the prompt and timely payment of salaries and other entitlements. Workers must not have to struggle or beg for what they have lawfully earned,” he said. The former civil servant also proposed a ₦9.6bn revolving loan scheme for market traders and another ₦9.6bn single-digit interest loan scheme for micro, small and medium-scale enterprises. He said his administration would establish a ₦3bn Women Enterprises and Empowerment Fund to provide affordable financing and business support to women-owned businesses, while at least 1,000 artisans would receive support grants annually. On grassroots development, Kawu promised to allocate ₦50m to each of the 193 wards in the state within the first 100 days of his administration, amounting to an initial commitment of ₦9.65bn. He said communities would determine their priority projects under the initiative, while mechanisms would be introduced to ensure transparency, technical supervision and accountability in their execution. The governorship candidate also proposed a ₦40bn One Kwara Regional Development Agency to drive infrastructure and community development, alongside a minimum of ₦5bn in counterpart funding for donor-supported projects over four years. He said his administration would prioritise the construction and rehabilitation of roads linking communities to markets, schools, hospitals and economic centres, while expanding rural electrification, renewable energy and access to clean water. On education, Kawu promised to commit ₦4bn to a special monthly hardship allowance for teachers serving in underserved, rural and hard-to-reach communities. He also pledged to rehabilitate dilapidated schools, provide teaching materials, improve teachers’ welfare and expand technical and vocational education, digital learning and scholarship opportunities for disadvantaged students. In the health sector, the PDP candidate promised to strengthen primary healthcare facilities across the 16 local government areas, improve access to essential medicines and introduce special allowances for qualified health workers serving in underserved communities. He also promised to establish an annual framework for youth employment and enterprise development, saying his administration would create 200,000 new youth employment opportunities and 5,000 enterprise opportunities yearly through skills acquisition, entrepreneurship support and private-sector partnerships. On agriculture, Kawu said the proposed ₦19.2bn production fund would provide farmers with affordable and timely financing, improved inputs and other forms of support to boost agricultural productivity. He further promised to address pension and gratuity obligations through a transparent repayment framework, with an estimated ₦4bn increase in payments over four years. The candidate also pledged to review upwards the salaries, allowances and other entitlements of traditional rulers, whom he described as important partners in maintaining social cohesion and promoting grassroots development. Explaining how he intended to finance and implement the proposals, Kawu said his administration would prioritise responsible planning and budgeting, efficient resource mobilisation, effective government systems, transparency and citizen participation. He said his experience in public service, particularly at the Rural Electrification Agency, had equipped him with the knowledge of project conception, design, implementation, monitoring and maintenance required to deliver the proposed programmes. Kawu also criticised what he described as the absence of proper planning in governance, saying he would not assume office without a clear programme of action. item.title: PHOTOS: Nigerian High Commissioner, others present Letters of Credence to Ghanaian President
item.description: President John Dramani Mahama of the Republic of Ghana has received Letters of Credence from the 11 newly appointed Ambassadors and High Commissioners. Diplomats from South Africa, Nigeria, India, Thailand, Lebanon, Australia, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Finland, Slovakia and Sweden presented their letters to the President at Jubilee House, Accra. Addressing the diplomatic representatives, President Mahama reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to deepening diplomatic engagement, strengthening bilateral relations and exploring new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation. He highlighted Ghana’s interest in strengthening its historical, political, cultural and economic ties with partner nations, while calling for greater international collaboration in advancing shared priorities, including Africa’s development, reparatory justice and investment opportunities.
